claim: The class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex I (PI3KC3-C1) that functions in early autophagy consists of the lipid kinase VPS34, the scaffolding protein VPS15, the tumor suppressor BECN1, and the autophagy-specific subunit ATG14.
source: The class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex I (PI3KC3-C1) that functions in early autophagy consists of the lipid kinase VPS34, the scaffolding protein VPS15, the tumor suppressor BECN1, and the autophagy-specific subunit ATG14.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the complex composition.

claim: The structure of the ATG14-containing PI3KC3-C1 was determined by single-particle EM, revealing a V-shaped architecture.
source: The structure of the ATG14-containing PI3KC3-C1 was determined by single-particle EM, revealing a V-shaped architecture.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by EM data shown in figures.

claim: All of the ordered domains of VPS34, VPS15, and BECN1 were mapped by MBP tagging.
source: All of the ordered domains of VPS34, VPS15, and BECN1 were mapped by MBP tagging.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: A novel 20-residue ordered region C-terminal to the VPS34 C2 domain was revealed by hydrogen–deuterium exchange.
source: The dynamics of the complex were defined using hydrogen–deuterium exchange, revealing a novel 20-residue ordered region C-terminal to the VPS34 C2 domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by HDX-MS data in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: VPS15 organizes the complex and serves as a bridge between VPS34 and the ATG14:BECN1 subcomplex.
source: VPS15 organizes the complex and serves as a bridge between VPS34 and the ATG14:BECN1 subcomplex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the structural model shown in Figure 5.

claim: Dynamic transitions occur in which the lipid kinase domain is ejected from the complex.
source: Dynamic transitions occur in which the lipid kinase domain is ejected from the complex and VPS15 pivots at the base of the V.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by 2D class averages shown in Figures 1D and 9.

claim: VPS15 pivots at the base of the V during dynamic transitions.
source: Dynamic transitions occur in which the lipid kinase domain is ejected from the complex and VPS15 pivots at the base of the V.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by 2D class averages shown in Figure 9.

claim: The N-terminus of BECN1, the target for signaling inputs, resides near the pivot point.
source: The N-terminus of BECN1, the target for signaling inputs, resides near the pivot point.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: Macroautophagy is a conserved eukaryotic pathway for cellular self-preservation through cellular self-consumption.
source: Macroautophagy (hereafter, 'autophagy') is a conserved eukaryotic pathway for cellular self-preservation through cellular self-consumption (Mizushima et al., 2011; Rubinsztein et al., 2012b; Reggiori and Klionsky, 2013; Green and Levine, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The most ancient role for autophagy is surviving during starvation.
source: The most ancient role for autophagy is surviving during starvation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: BECN1 is a tumor suppressor.
source: For example, the core autophagy protein BECN1 (Beclin 1) is a tumor suppressor.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: BECN1 is deleted in 40–75% of human breast, ovarian, and prostate cancers.
source: BECN1 is deleted in 40–75% of human breast, ovarian, and prostate cancers (Liang et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Autophagy protects cells from the accumulation of pathogenic inclusions that can lead to Huntington's, Parkinson's, and other neurodegenerative diseases under most conditions.
source: Autophagy is also thought, under most conditions, to protect cells from the accumulation of pathogenic inclusions that can lead to Huntington's, Parkinson's, and other neurodegenerative diseases (Rubinsztein et al., 2012a; Nixon, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: During the initiation of autophagy, an autophagy-specific form of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex (PI3KC3-C1) is activated and recruited to the site of phagophore nucleation.
source: During the initiation of autophagy, an autophagy-specific form of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex (PI3KC3-C1) is activated and recruited to the site of phagophore nucleation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Class III PI3Ks synthesize phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI(3)P) from phosphatidylinositol (PI).
source: Class III PI3Ks synthesize phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI(3)P) from phosphatidylinositol (PI), as compared to the class I and II PI3Ks that generate PI(3,4,5)P3 and PI(3,4)P2, respectively (Backer, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Class I PI3Ks generate PI(3,4,5)P3.
source: Class III PI3Ks synthesize phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI(3)P) from phosphatidylinositol (PI), as compared to the class I and II PI3Ks that generate PI(3,4,5)P3 and PI(3,4)P2, respectively (Backer, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Class II PI3Ks generate PI(3,4)P2.
source: Class III PI3Ks synthesize phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI(3)P) from phosphatidylinositol (PI), as compared to the class I and II PI3Ks that generate PI(3,4,5)P3 and PI(3,4)P2, respectively (Backer, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: In yeast, there are two PI 3-kinase complexes, known as complexes I and II, with clear-cut distinctions in their functions.
source: In yeast, where the complex was first characterized, there are two PI 3-kinase complexes, known as complexes I and II, with clear-cut distinctions in their functions (Kihara et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Both yeast complexes contain the core subunits Vps34, Vps15, and Atg6.
source: Both yeast complexes contain the core subunits Vps34, Vps15, and Atg6.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Vps34 contains the catalytic domain responsible for lipid kinase activity.
source: Vps34 contains the catalytic domain responsible for lipid kinase activity, as well as a putative lipid-binding C2 domain and a helical domain (Schu et al., 1993; Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Vps34 contains a putative lipid-binding C2 domain.
source: Vps34 contains the catalytic domain responsible for lipid kinase activity, as well as a putative lipid-binding C2 domain and a helical domain (Schu et al., 1993; Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Vps34 contains a helical domain.
source: Vps34 contains the catalytic domain responsible for lipid kinase activity, as well as a putative lipid-binding C2 domain and a helical domain (Schu et al., 1993; Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Vps15 is a large (150 kDa) protein essential for the activity of the complex.
source: Vps15 is a large (150 kDa) protein essential for the activity of the complex (Stack et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Vps15 contains a protein kinase domain whose function and possible substrates are uncertain.
source: Vps15 contains a protein kinase domain whose function and possible substrates are uncertain, as well as HEAT and WD40 repeats.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as current knowledge.

claim: Vps15 contains HEAT repeats.
source: Vps15 contains a protein kinase domain whose function and possible substrates are uncertain, as well as HEAT and WD40 repeats.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Vps15 contains WD40 repeats.
source: Vps15 contains a protein kinase domain whose function and possible substrates are uncertain, as well as HEAT and WD40 repeats.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Atg6 is the yeast ortholog of the human tumor suppressor BECN1.
source: Atg6 is the yeast ortholog of the human tumor suppressor BECN1 and contains an intrinsically disordered region, a coiled coil, and a BARA domain.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Atg6 contains an intrinsically disordered region.
source: Atg6 is the yeast ortholog of the human tumor suppressor BECN1 and contains an intrinsically disordered region, a coiled coil, and a BARA domain.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Atg6 contains a coiled coil.
source: Atg6 is the yeast ortholog of the human tumor suppressor BECN1 and contains an intrinsically disordered region, a coiled coil, and a BARA domain.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Atg6 contains a BARA domain.
source: Atg6 is the yeast ortholog of the human tumor suppressor BECN1 and contains an intrinsically disordered region, a coiled coil, and a BARA domain.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Yeast complex I contains the coiled coil subunit Atg14 and is the complex that is involved in autophagy initiation.
source: Yeast complex I further contains the coiled coil subunit Atg14 and is the complex that is involved in autophagy initiation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Yeast complex II contains the coiled coil protein Vps38 and functions in endosome maturation.
source: Yeast complex II contains instead another coiled coil protein, Vps38, and functions in endosome maturation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The yeast complexes are prototypes of two human PI 3-kinase complexes.
source: The yeast complexes are prototypes of two human PI 3-kinase complexes (Volinia et al., 1995), which both contain the common core subunits VPS34 (also known as PI3KC3), VPS15, and BECN1 (Backer, 2008; Funderburk et al., 2010; He and Levine, 2010; Wirth et al., 2013) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Both human PI 3-kinase complexes contain the common core subunits VPS34, VPS15, and BECN1.
source: The yeast complexes are prototypes of two human PI 3-kinase complexes (Volinia et al., 1995), which both contain the common core subunits VPS34 (also known as PI3KC3), VPS15, and BECN1 (Backer, 2008; Funderburk et al., 2010; He and Levine, 2010; Wirth et al., 2013) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The human cognate of PI3KC3 complex I contains ATG14.
source: The human cognate of PI3KC3 complex I contains ATG14 (also known as ATG14L or BARKOR) (Itakura et al., 2008; Sun et al., 2008; Matsunaga et al., 2009; Zhong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: ATG14 is specifically recruited to sites of autophagosome initiation.
source: ATG14 is specifically recruited to sites of autophagosome initiation (Matsunaga et al., 2010; Fogel et al., 2013; Graef et al., 2013; Hamasaki et al., 2013; Wirth et al., 2013; Ge et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: A second human PI3KC3 contains UVRAG in place of ATG14.
source: A second human PI3KC3 contains, in place of ATG14, the UV resistance-associated gene product, UVRAG.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: PI3KC3-C2 has been proposed to function at later stages in autophagy.
source: PI3KC3-C2 has been proposed to function at later stages in autophagy (Liang et al., 2006) but is not currently thought to participate in the initiation of autophagosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: PI3KC3-C2 is not currently thought to participate in the initiation of autophagosome biogenesis.
source: PI3KC3-C2 has been proposed to function at later stages in autophagy (Liang et al., 2006) but is not currently thought to participate in the initiation of autophagosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as current knowledge.

claim: Crystal structures have been obtained for the catalytic core and helical domains of Drosophila Vps34.
source: To date, crystal structures have been obtained for the catalytic core and helical domains of Drosophila Vps34 (Miller et al., 2010), the WD40 propeller domain of yeast Vps15 (Heenan et al., 2009), the coiled coil domain of human BECN1 (Li et al., 2012), and the BARA domains of yeast and human Atg6/BECN1 (Huang et al., 2012; Noda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Crystal structures have been obtained for the WD40 propeller domain of yeast Vps15.
source: To date, crystal structures have been obtained for the catalytic core and helical domains of Drosophila Vps34 (Miller et al., 2010), the WD40 propeller domain of yeast Vps15 (Heenan et al., 2009), the coiled coil domain of human BECN1 (Li et al., 2012), and the BARA domains of yeast and human Atg6/BECN1 (Huang et al., 2012; Noda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Crystal structures have been obtained for the coiled coil domain of human BECN1.
source: To date, crystal structures have been obtained for the catalytic core and helical domains of Drosophila Vps34 (Miller et al., 2010), the WD40 propeller domain of yeast Vps15 (Heenan et al., 2009), the coiled coil domain of human BECN1 (Li et al., 2012), and the BARA domains of yeast and human Atg6/BECN1 (Huang et al., 2012; Noda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Crystal structures have been obtained for the BARA domains of yeast and human Atg6/BECN1.
source: To date, crystal structures have been obtained for the catalytic core and helical domains of Drosophila Vps34 (Miller et al., 2010), the WD40 propeller domain of yeast Vps15 (Heenan et al., 2009), the coiled coil domain of human BECN1 (Li et al., 2012), and the BARA domains of yeast and human Atg6/BECN1 (Huang et al., 2012; Noda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: PI3KC3-C1 has a molecular weight of 361.8 kDa.
source: Currently, there are essentially no data on the structure of the 361.8 kDa quaternary assembly of these subunits with each other in PI3KC3-C1 (Hurley and Schulman, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Active human PI3KC3-C1 was reconstituted by co-expression of all four subunits.
source: To this end, we reconstituted active human PI3KC3-C1 and PI3KC3-C2 by co-expression of all four subunits and imaged the complex by electron microscopy (EM).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Active human PI3KC3-C2 was reconstituted by co-expression of all four subunits.
source: To this end, we reconstituted active human PI3KC3-C1 and PI3KC3-C2 by co-expression of all four subunits and imaged the complex by electron microscopy (EM).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: The complexes are elongated, loosely connected, and dynamic.
source: The complexes are elongated, loosely connected, and dynamic; yet by careful selection of class averages and Bayesian data processing, we were able to generate a three-dimensional reconstruction of PI3KC3-C1 at 28-Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by EM data in Figures 1, 3, and 9.

claim: A three-dimensional reconstruction of PI3KC3-C1 at 28-Å resolution was generated.
source: The complexes are elongated, loosely connected, and dynamic; yet by careful selection of class averages and Bayesian data processing, we were able to generate a three-dimensional reconstruction of PI3KC3-C1 at 28-Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by EM data in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: The positions of the various domains of the subunits were mapped by tagging with maltose binding protein (MBP).
source: We have mapped the positions of the various domains of the subunits by tagging with maltose binding protein (MBP).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: The main architectural principles hold for both PI3KC3-C1 and PI3KC3-C2 complexes.
source: The main architectural principles also hold for the PI3KC3-C2 complex.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by 2D class averages in Figure 6.

claim: The VPS15 kinase domain acts as a latch to regulate PI 3-kinase activity in both the PI3KC3-C1 and -C2.
source: The structural model suggests that the VPS15 kinase domain acts as a latch to regulate PI 3-kinase activity in both the PI3KC3-C1 and -C2.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a speculation based on the structural model.

claim: The reconstituted PI3KC3-C1 complex contained all four subunits at apparently equal stoichiometry.
source: The resulting complex contained all four subunits at apparently equal stoichiometry (Figure 1B) and the subunits co-migrated as a single peak on gel filtration chromatography (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by SDS-PAGE data in Figure 1B.

claim: The subunits of PI3KC3-C1 co-migrated as a single peak on gel filtration chromatography.
source: The resulting complex contained all four subunits at apparently equal stoichiometry (Figure 1B) and the subunits co-migrated as a single peak on gel filtration chromatography (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by gel filtration data in Figure 2A.

claim: The reconstituted PI3KC3-C1 was enzymatically active as judged by ATP hydrolysis in the presence of PI.
source: The material was enzymatically active as judged by ATP hydrolysis in the presence of PI (Figure 2B) and by the formation of PI(3)P from PI as assessed by thin layer chromatography (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ATP hydrolysis data in Figure 2B.

claim: The reconstituted PI3KC3-C1 was enzymatically active as judged by the formation of PI(3)P from PI.
source: The material was enzymatically active as judged by ATP hydrolysis in the presence of PI (Figure 2B) and by the formation of PI(3)P from PI as assessed by thin layer chromatography (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by TLC data in Figure 1C.

claim: ATP hydrolysis by PI3KC3-C1 was essentially completely blocked by the PI 3-kinase inhibitor wortmannin.
source: ATP hydrolysis by PI3KC3-C1 was essentially completely blocked by the PI 3-kinase inhibitor wortmannin (Figure 2B), confirming that the ATPase activity was due to the lipid kinase domain and not either the VPS15 kinase domain or contaminants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by inhibition data in Figure 2B.

claim: The ATPase activity of PI3KC3-C1 was due to the lipid kinase domain and not the VPS15 kinase domain or contaminants.
source: ATP hydrolysis by PI3KC3-C1 was essentially completely blocked by the PI 3-kinase inhibitor wortmannin (Figure 2B), confirming that the ATPase activity was due to the lipid kinase domain and not either the VPS15 kinase domain or contaminants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by wortmannin inhibition data in Figure 2B.

claim: Two-dimensional class averages for PI3KC3-C1 revealed a V-shaped particle with two arms of approximately 20 nm in length.
source: Two-dimensional class averages for PI3KC3-C1 are shown in Figure 1D. The class averages revealed a V-shaped particle with two arms of approximately 20 nm in length.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by 2D class averages in Figure 1D.

claim: There was a strongly preferred orientation with the V view visible face-on in projection.
source: There was a strongly preferred orientation with the V view visible face-on in projection (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Euler angle distribution in Figure 3B.

claim: An ab initio 3D reconstruction was generated by the random conical tilt (RCT) method.
source: An ab initio 3D reconstruction was generated by the random conical tilt (RCT) method (Radermacher et al., 1987) and refined using particles acquired at 0°, 30°, and 45°.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The chirality of the structure was validated by tilt-pair analysis.
source: The chirality of the structure was validated by tilt-pair analysis (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003) with image pairs collected at 0° and 15° (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by tilt-pair analysis in Figure 3D.

claim: Both N- and C-terminal MBP fusions of VPS34 and BECN1 were successfully purified and imaged.
source: Both N- and C-terminal MBP fusions of VPS34 and BECN1 and the N-terminal MBP fusions of ATG14 and VPS15 were successfully purified and imaged.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: The N-terminal MBP fusions of ATG14 and VPS15 were successfully purified and imaged.
source: Both N- and C-terminal MBP fusions of VPS34 and BECN1 and the N-terminal MBP fusions of ATG14 and VPS15 were successfully purified and imaged.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: The VPS34 kinase subunit is at the tip of the right-hand arm of the V.
source: With respect to the canonical 'V' view of the complex, the VPS34 kinase subunit is at the tip of the right-hand arm of the V.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: The N-terminus of VPS34 is near the crotch of the V.
source: With respect to the canonical 'V' view of the complex, the VPS34 kinase subunit is at the tip of the right-hand arm of the V. Its N-terminus is near the crotch of the V.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: BECN1 is aligned with the left arm of the complex.
source: In turn, BECN1 is aligned with the left arm of the complex.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: The N-terminus of BECN1 is near the junction of the V.
source: In turn, BECN1 is aligned with the left arm of the complex. Its N-terminus is near the junction of the V and its C-terminus at the tip of the left arm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: The C-terminus of BECN1 is at the tip of the left arm.
source: In turn, BECN1 is aligned with the left arm of the complex. Its N-terminus is near the junction of the V and its C-terminus at the tip of the left arm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: The N-terminus of scaffolding VPS15 subunit is located near the C-terminus of VPS34 in the right arm.
source: The N-terminus of scaffolding VPS15 subunit is located near the C-terminus of VPS34 in the right arm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: The N-terminus of ATG14 is near that of BECN1.
source: Finally, the N-terminus of ATG14 is near that of BECN1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by MBP tagging data in Figure 4.

claim: The BECN1 and ATG14 coiled coils must be parallel to each other.
source: Strikingly, this suggests that the BECN1 and ATG14 coiled coils must be parallel to each other, in contrast to the antiparallel coiled coil described for the BECN1 homodimer (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from MBP tagging data.

claim: The BECN1 homodimer forms an antiparallel coiled coil.
source: Strikingly, this suggests that the BECN1 and ATG14 coiled coils must be parallel to each other, in contrast to the antiparallel coiled coil described for the BECN1 homodimer (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The docked volume accounted for 65% of the total density.
source: Given the added guidance provided by MBP tags, we docked the known crystal structures or homology models of the structured domains of VPS34, VPS15, and BECN1 on to the density and the docked volume accounted for 65% of the total density. (Figure 5A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the docked model in Figure 5.

claim: The helical and catalytic domains of VPS34 are integrated into a single structural unit referred to as the 'HELCAT' region.
source: The helical and catalytic domains of VPS34 are integrated into a single structural unit referred to as the 'HELCAT' region (Miller et al., 2010) (Figure 1A), which matches in size and shape the density identified near the C-terminal MBP tag in this subunit (Figures 4B and 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: A density feature matching the size and shape of the C2 domain is located between the HELCAT and the N-terminal MBP tag.
source: A density feature matching the size and shape of the C2 domain is located between the HELCAT and the N-terminal MBP tag (Figures 4B and 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the EM density in Figure 5.

claim: A model based on the structure of the C2 domain of PI3KC2α was docked into the VPS34 C2 density, and a reasonable fit was obtained.
source: However, a model based on the closely related structure of the C2 domain of PI3KC2α (Liu et al., 2006) was docked into this density, and a reasonable fit was obtained (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The crystal structure of the BARA domain of human BECN1 was unambiguously identified as a match to the density feature near the BECN1 C-terminal MBP tag.
source: The crystal structure of the BARA domain (also sometimes referred to as the 'ECD') of human BECN1 (Huang et al., 2012) was unambiguously identified as a match to the size and shape of the only density feature near the BECN1 C-terminal MBP tag (Figures 4B and 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: A homology model for the VPS15 kinase catalytic domain was derived from the structure of protein kinase A (PKA).
source: A homology model for the VPS15 kinase catalytic domain was derived from the structure of protein kinase A (PKA) (Knighton et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: A model for the 498-residue HEAT repeat domain of VPS15 was generated by threading the corresponding sequence onto the backbone of the HEAT repeat portion of the exportin subunit Cse1.
source: A model for the 498-residue HEAT repeat domain of VPS15 was generated by threading the corresponding sequence onto the backbone of the HEAT repeat portion of the exportin subunit Cse1 (Matsuura and Stewart, 2004) and provided an excellent match to the arch-shaped density adjoining the C-terminus of the VPS15 kinase domain (Figures 4B and 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The kinase and HEAT repeat domains of VPS15 seem to be fused into a single contiguous unit.
source: Indeed, the kinase and HEAT repeat domains of VPS15 seem to be fused into a single contiguous unit.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the structural model.

claim: The WD40 propeller region of VPS15 is connected to the HEAT by a 180-residue linker.
source: The most C-terminal domain of VPS15, the WD40 propeller region, is connected to the HEAT by a 180-residue linker.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a description of the domain architecture.

claim: The WD40 propeller of VPS15 was assigned to a density feature located next to the BECN1 BARA domain, which has a donut-like shape that matches the crystal structure of the yeast Vps15 propeller domain.
source: This propeller was assigned to the last unaccounted for density feature, located next to the BECN1 BARA domain, which has a donut-like shape that matches the crystal structure of the yeast Vps15 propeller domain (Heenan et al., 2009) (Figures 4B and 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The docked or assigned regions of the VPS34 C2 and HELCAT, VPS15 kinase, HEAT, and WD40, BECN1 BARA domains account for 2162 residues of the 3187 present in ATG14–PI3KC3.
source: Collectively, the docked or assigned regions of the VPS34 C2 and HELCAT, VPS15 kinase, HEAT, and WD40, BECN1 BARA domains account for 2162 residues of the 3187 present in ATG14–PI3KC3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the docking analysis.

claim: Two long, narrow tubes of density are present in the area where the ATG14 and BECN1 coiled coil regions would be expected.
source: Two long, narrow tubes of density are present in the area where the ATG14 and BECN1 coiled coil regions would be expected (Figure 5A,D third panel, see arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A,D.

claim: One tube of density is adjacent to the VPS15 WD40 domain and points towards the BECN1 BARA domain at one end and towards the second tube at the other.
source: One tube is adjacent to the VPS15 WD40 domain. It points towards the BECN1 BARA domain at one end and towards the second tube at the other.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a description of the density features.

claim: Following a gap in the density between the two tubes, the second tube continues until it merges with the density for the VPS15 HEAT domains.
source: Following a gap in the density between the two tubes, the second one continues until it merges with the density for the VPS15 HEAT domains.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a description of the density features.

claim: The tubular density region was assigned to the coiled coil dimer of ATG14 and BECN1.
source: The BARA domain marks the C-terminus of the BECN1 coiled-coil, and MBP marks the N-termini of ATG14 and BECN1 coils, so we assigned this region to the coiled coil dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural data.

claim: One of the unassigned density features projects away from the VPS15 HEAT domain, very near the MBP markers for the N-termini of ATG14 and BECN1.
source: One of the few unassigned density features projects away from the VPS15 HEAT domain (Figure 5A,C), very near the MBP markers for the N-termini of ATG14 and BECN1 (Figure 4B).
